clue.text: Henry's blue? What happened?

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance, and 's stands for 'is'
blue is the colour of the UK Conservatives, so a blue is a Tory

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a man called Henry is feeling down, and what has gone on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry's' splits as H (the henry, a unit of inductance) plus 'S read as IS; a blue is a Tory, the Conservatives being Britain's blue party.
explanation.definitionFit: The past, everything that has occurred, is what the study of bygone events records.

clue.text: Welcoming speech head of economics provided for institute

indicators.note: one letter is supplied in place of another, so the new letter stands for the old

parts.note: a homily is a moralising speech or sermon

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A friendly address in which an economics chief stands in for the institute's own speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided for' means the E from 'head of economics' replaces the I (institute) in HOMILY.
explanation.definitionFit: A homely place feels cosy and comfortable, which is how a welcoming one feels to guests.

clue.text: Abandons second game

parts.note: craps is a dice game

explanation.surface: Someone gives up after a second match.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrap a plan is to drop or discard it, a close synonym of giving it up.

clue.text: Australian chap stops Daisy upsetting mummy

parts.note: Oz is informal for Australia, so Australian gives OZ

indicators.note: the man word plugs a gap in the other letters, stopping them up like a cork
upsetting the letters of the name throws them into a new order

parts.note: a chap is a man

explanation.surface: An Australian bloke gets in the way of Daisy, who is upsetting her mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' gives YDIAS, which 'stops' splits after its first letter. 'mummy' looks like a mother but means an embalmed pharaoh.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozymandias is the Greek name for the pharaoh Ramesses II, whose embalmed remains survive; Shelley's sonnet made the name famous.

clue.text: A bear caught posturing?

parts.note: Yogi Bear is the cartoon bear of Jellystone Park
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A bear that has been captured seems to be striking poses.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'posturing' is meant literally: holding yoga postures.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoga is built on holding bodily positions, so posturing in that sense is the practice of that discipline.

clue.text: American actress at university still?

parts.note: Glenn Close is an American actress
to be up is to be in residence at university

explanation.surface: Asks whether a US actress is still a student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' reads as 'yet', but here it is a noun: a single photograph or film frame. In Britain you are 'up' at university.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightly framed single shot of a face is a kind of photograph, hence a still, with the question mark marking the example.

clue.text: Mixture of more than 50% Rochelle salt and different salts

indicators.note: a mixture blends things together, so the letters are stirred into a new order
a bit more than half of the word, its first five of eight letters, is used

explanation.surface: A chemistry recipe: combine over half Rochelle salt with a different salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more than 50%' takes ROCHE from Rochelle; 'Mixture of' scrambles ROCHE with SALT. Rochelle salt is a real compound, which disguises the mechanics.
explanation.definitionFit: These are compounds containing the ClO3 ion, a family of various chemical salts.

clue.text: Leader in Syrian city moves resistance units

indicators.note: the leader of the city's name, its first letter, is the one taken out
the letter shifts to a new spot in the same word

parts.note: Homs is a city in western Syria

explanation.surface: A political leader relocates within a Syrian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader in ... moves' sends the H at the head of HOMS to second place.
explanation.definitionFit: The ohm is the SI measure of electrical resistance, so these are its units in the plural.

clue.text: Knock out the bastard on top of Eiffel Tower

indicators.note: something bastard is impure or corrupted, so these letters are garbled
in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to tower is to rise up high

explanation.surface: An order to knock some villain out atop the Eiffel Tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bastard' makes ETH from THE; 'top of Eiffel' gives E; 'Tower' is a verb, RISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was the classic anaesthetic, so to treat someone with it is to render them unconscious.

clue.text: Get a leather on the ear

indicators.note: the words are taken as heard, not as written

parts.note: per means a or each, as in once per day; suede is a soft leather

explanation.surface: Instructions to fetch a leather and put it on someone's ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the ear' says it is heard: 'per' (a, each) plus 'suede' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To get someone to do something is to talk them into it, coaxing their agreement.

clue.text: Relief from the unipolar economic ideology at last

indicators.note: the final letter of each word in the run is taken

explanation.surface: Finally there is respite from a one-sided economic doctrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' takes the last letters of 'from', 'the', 'unipolar', 'economic', 'ideology'.
explanation.definitionFit: Clemency or compassion brings release from suffering, as in a mercy granted to the condemned.

clue.text: Clumsy type, awfully large, going round university at speed

indicators.note: the jumbled letters encircle the other pieces
done awfully, the letters come out in a wrong, jumbled order

parts.note: MPH, miles per hour, measures speed

explanation.surface: A big, ungainly person races round a campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' scrambles to GALER, which 'going round' splits after GA; 'at' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To galumph is to move heavily and noisily, so one who does it is an awkward, lumbering person.

clue.text: Landscaper gets aroused by erotic performers

indicators.note: aroused letters are stirred up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A gardener finds himself excited by strippers.
explanation.definitionFit: These are dancers who perform close to or on a seated customer at a strip club.

clue.text: Duke abandoned by cheating wife

indicators.note: the letter is left out, dropped from the longer word

parts.note: fraud is cheating or deception

explanation.surface: An unfaithful wife leaves her duke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned by' takes D (duke) out of FRAUD.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the German term for a married woman, used like Mrs or for one's spouse.

clue.text: Two princes left concert venue

parts.note: Prince Albert, Victoria's consort, and Prince Hal, Shakespeare's young Henry V

explanation.surface: Two royals have departed from a concert venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a verb but is just L.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Albert Hall in London is a famous concert hall, home of the Proms.

clue.text: Enjoy sex with naughty ladies prepared to go on the internet?

definitions.text: prepared to go on the internet?

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking it
it is slang for sex

indicators.note: naughty letters misbehave and fall out of order

explanation.surface: Enjoying sex with racy women who are ready to appear online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' rearranges LADIES as ALISED.
explanation.definitionFit: Converting material into electronic form readies it for computers and online use.

clue.text: Cricketing legend (not English) makes embellishment to score

parts.note: W.G. Grace was the great Victorian English cricketer

explanation.surface: A great cricketer, not English, adds polish to his batting total.
explanation.walkthrough: W.G. Grace is cricket's Victorian giant. '(not English)' gives NOT plus E. 'score' suggests runs but means a piece of written music.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental extra note added to a melody decorates the written music.

clue.text: Begins to drink after eating pies

indicators.note: the drink word takes the pies inside it, as if swallowing them

parts.note: to sup is to drink
tarts are open pies

explanation.surface: Someone starts drinking once the pies are eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after eating' reads as time order but signals containment: the drink swallows the pies. 'Begins' alone is the definition; 'to' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means sets something going, a phrasal verb for commencing or launching.

clue.text: Charlie has to hang around with son inside arcade

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the abbreviation for son goes within the loitering word

parts.note: to loiter is to hang around idly

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie must wait about with his son in a shopping arcade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts S within LOITER, after C. 'arcade' suggests shops, but means a covered walkway.
explanation.definitionFit: A covered walk with a colonnade, typically round a monastery courtyard, is an arched passage.

clue.text: Incredible adult experiences with 20 in US city

parts.note: a tall story is an incredible one
A is the old film-certificate abbreviation for adult
to have something, as in has fun, is to experience it
20 down is ESCORT, and to see someone home is to escort them

explanation.surface: A grown-up has an unbelievable time with a companion in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: '20' points to 20 down; 'see' (as in see someone out) shares its meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallahassee is the state capital of Florida, a city in the United States.

clue.text: Fetish about vermouth cocktail

indicators.note: the charm word goes around the vermouth

parts.note: a mojo is a magic charm or fetish
It, short for Italian, is sweet vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: Someone's obsession with vermouth extends to a mixed drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts IT inside MOJO; 'It' is British shorthand for Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: This Cuban mixed drink of rum, lime, mint and soda is a classic mixed drink.

clue.text: Car attendant

definitions.meaning: the Ford ... was a popular car model
someone who accompanies another as a guard or companion

explanation.definitionFit: A Ford model name, and also a companion who goes along with someone for protection.

clue.text: Croatians regularly shower

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every second one

explanation.surface: People from Croatia take a shower as a habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of Croatians.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief fall of drops from clouds is a shower of precipitation.

clue.text: What discounter could provide

indicators.note: the letters of the word could be rearranged to supply something else

explanation.surface: Asks what a cut-price retailer might offer.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'discounter', rearranged, give the answer, which is also what a discounter offers.
explanation.definitionFit: A discount shop sells at lowered prices, so price cuts are what it hands out.

clue.text: Ken after standing goes below

indicators.note: the part leaves, removed from the longer word

parts.note: to ken is to know or comprehend, a Scots verb
to be standing is to stand

explanation.surface: A man named Ken, after standing a while, goes downstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ken' is not a man but the verb 'to know'; once STAND 'goes', the rest remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Beneath and lower than something, the two prepositions are synonyms.

clue.text: This card game takes the biscuit

definitions.meaning: a children's card game where players call out on matching cards
a ginger biscuit is called a ginger ...

explanation.surface: A card game is declared the most outrageous of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes the biscuit' is a British idiom for being the most outrageous, but the biscuit is the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game shouted when matching cards appear, and a thin crisp biscuit, as in gingersnap.

clue.text: Perched with forest wolf in a tree

indicators.note: to wolf is to gulp down, so the outer letters swallow the small word

parts.note: to have perched is to have sat
a wood is a small forest

explanation.surface: Perched in a tree beside a wolf from the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wolf' looks like an animal but is the verb, to gulp down, signalling containment.
explanation.definitionFit: This East Indian or West Indian tree yields a lustrous yellowish timber, used in fine furniture.

clue.text: A fighter plane heading round China

parts.note: the MiG is a Russian fighter plane
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A fighter jet heads around China on a mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading' just links: the plane is heading round. 'China' means friend: 'china plate' is Cockney rhyming slang for mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a pal: one Spanish, the other Cockney rhyming slang for mate.

clue.text: The story of a meat product

definitions.meaning: a story can be a lie, and ... is Cockney rhyming slang for lie
a pastry filled with chopped pork

explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang for a lie, and a pastry case of pork served cold.

clue.text: Dismiss the possibility of rugby stars attending do

parts.note: RU is short for Rugby Union
Leo is a constellation, a group of stars
ut is the old name for the note do in sol-fa

explanation.surface: Rugby players attending a party make it impossible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' is not a party but the musical note, whose older name is ut.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclude an option is to eliminate it from consideration.
